title: One promise we will not move
narration: A repairer cancels, but a visitor's promised slot must stay. This synthetic example lets an organizer and browser agent inspect the consequences before applying a new plan.

title: Real native WebMCP · fixed rehearsal script
narration: Now Sam cancels. These are real browser native Web M C P calls, driven by a fixed script. No language model is choosing tools in this recording. The script reads the event and stages a proposal.

title: Current and proposed plans stay separate
narration: The lamp stays at ten. The current plan is untouched. We can compare the proposed timeline with the current one, then inspect exactly who moves and who still has no appointment.

title: Explain a missing slot, not just a failure
narration: The fan needs more than a generic failure message. A native tool checks eligible start times and explains the smallest local displacement. Those other visitors have not yet been replanned. A possible opening is not a complete solution.

title: Make room for one item · inspect the cost
narration: Now make room for the fan. The full counterfactual shows the cost: which appointments move or lose a slot. Protected promises and reserved walk in time remain fixed. The current event still has not changed.

title: Review the exact proposal in the human interface
narration: There is no apply or unlock tool. The final decision is made in this review interface. Its confirmation is bound to the exact proposal. Applying changes only the local plan and sends no messages.

title: Current-plan handoff · no visitors contacted
narration: Print a reception sheet and copies for volunteers, or download a backup. The same product works manually without Web M C P. It plans time and exposes trade offs. It does not promise that every repair will succeed.
